claims.text: In CrFeCoNiAl alloys above 900 °C, preferential segregation of Al at the oxide/alloy interface controls the formation and persistence of a protective oxide.
Interfacial Al segregation promotes formation of an ultra-thin Al-rich oxide.
The Al-rich interfacial oxide acts as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
The Al-rich interfacial oxide acts as a diffusion barrier to outward-moving metal cations.
Formation of the Al-rich interfacial oxide reduces thermal-expansion mismatch and intrinsic oxide-growth stresses.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi are less able than CrFeCoNiAl to form the beneficial interfacial oxide.
The inability to form the Al-rich interfacial layer makes Mn- or Si-containing scales more prone to cracking and spallation during prolonged high-temperature exposure.
The proposed test material is homogenized CrFeCoNiAl in a single-phase or multiphase solid-solution state.
The controlled comparison uses CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi processed and exposed under conditions equivalent to those used for CrFeCoNiAl.
Exposure at or above 900 °C in a controlled oxidative or corrosive atmosphere causes Al to segregate to the oxide/alloy interface.
Restriction of oxygen and cation transport lowers oxide-growth kinetics.
Lower thermal-expansion mismatch and internal stress reduce oxide cracking and spallation.
CrFeCoNiAl will form a slower-growing, coherent, adherent, and protective oxide scale during high-temperature exposure.
CrFeCoNiMn and CrFeCoNiSi will form thicker and less adherent scales that crack and spall more readily than the scale on CrFeCoNiAl.
The proposed service domain is exposure above 900 °C for at least 100 hours in a controlled oxidative or corrosive atmosphere.
The hypothesis does not cover effects of prior thermomechanical processing or significant microstructural inhomogeneity.
Failure of CrFeCoNiAl to exhibit a thinner, more coherent, more adherent, Al-rich scale with lower oxidation kinetics than both comparators would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field includes multiphase alloys and the boundary appears to claim validity for the stated initial-state domain, but the uncertainty field says the effect of multiphase microstructures remains to be established. The intended phase-state scope is therefore internally inconsistent or at least unresolved.
